study.question: Does a fourth, count-weighted orthogonal quadratic block-order/value moment improve click prediction beyond the incumbent linear moments, extra duplicate capacity, and a scrambled-order projection under fixed task routing?
study.hypothesis: The incumbent preserves target-match covariance, within-block linear order and between-block linear order, but its summary path discards coarse curvature: histories with equal block means and linear value moments can differ in middle-versus-end composition. A masked quadratic coefficient orthogonal to the constant and linear block coefficients can expose this missing contrast to the existing target/context-conditioned task adapter. This is an information-loss hypothesis, not a claim that the whole model is invariant (nonlinear block scoring may already recover some signal).

nearest_work.difference: Preserve its first three moments and add a fourth orthogonal quadratic summary; task routing and gradient ownership are fixed.
Retain target-conditioned local activation as adapted in the incumbent; add fixed masked ordinal moments and task-conditioned correction. This is not an exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark forward flattens history and context before tokenization/mixing. Proposed code retains compressed scoring and exposes one low-dimensional fixed order moment; no flattened tokenizer or paired-stream mixer is adopted.

Original detailed text unavailable via authorized registry. Explicit benchmark fallback describes local Transformer compression and recent-query interaction; proposed statistic uses no Transformer and no separately supplied recent-query input. Stronger priority comparison remains unverified.

inherited_components: Incumbent FeatureEmbeddingDict and six item fields plus historical action; masks and target-match special-ID exclusions
Thirty uniform/feedback-stratified block slots and action-aware DIN scorer
Unchanged target-match, within-block position and between-block linear summary formulas
Four separate towers, task-specific zero-output-initialized residual bank, residual_hidden16
Source-specific auxiliary stop gradients and cloned Dice buffers
study.proposed_difference: Append one fourth summary to the residual features. Compute centered squared block ranks, remove their count-weighted projection on the valid linear block ranks, and scale coefficient norm to the incumbent coarse coefficient. A shared support gate requires at least three occupied blocks and finite nondegenerate true/scrambled residual norms. Replacement cells use either the gated inherited coarse coefficients (duplicate information), or a fixed permutation of squared block ranks projected off the SAME valid constant/linear basis. All cells build every coefficient and contract four channels. Freeze task routing; no interaction-with-routing claim is made.
predictions: Quadratic curvature_task exceeds both duplicate_linear_task and scrambled_curvature_task on full validation click AUC and exceeds incumbent0.6650111217270684 at a justified measured cost. Gains below0.0002 versus each matched control will be treated as weak/exploratory even if positive.

For valid histories spanning fewer than three blocks the fourth channel is exactly zero in every cell. Its coefficient sum and dot product with the unscaled inherited coarse rank are zero up to FP32 error in quadratic/scrambled cells.
Global value shifts and blockwise value trends affine in block ordinal cancel from the quadratic and scrambled fourth summaries. The duplicate channel has no new block-moment information.

Exploratory gains should concentrate in history_gt64 and history_17_64 rather than empty_history; coarse bins do not identify exact support. Empty-history prediction changes after training can arise from shared training, and are not direct curvature effects.
falsifiers: If quadratic does not exceed duplicate at matched capacity, useful missing-curvature information is unsupported for this implementation.

If quadratic and scrambled give indistinguishable gains over duplicate, an additional generic projection or optimization effect is a sufficient alternative; chronological-curvature specificity is unsupported.
If duplicate alone explains improvement over the three-channel incumbent, attribute the gain to added parameterization/optimization rather than a new statistic.
Any mask, finite-gradient, detached auxiliary-item path or inference discrepancy failure blocks interpretation and must be repaired within the same frozen protocol; charge failed host attempts.
A click gain with worse auxiliary metrics is a click-selected tradeoff, not an across-task improvement; the adapted DIN baseline already has substantially stronger auxiliary AUCs.
alternative_explanations: Single fixed seed, validation reuse/adaptive selection and initialization changes caused by widening the adapter first layer
Different coefficient distributions despite equal norm and common support; scrambled is a replacement diagnostic, not a perfect randomization of chronology
Static embeddings and nonlinear existing scorer may already encode a portion of coarse curvature; summary-only identifiability does not imply whole-model invariance
Fixed prepadding and clipping make ordinals differ from elapsed time; history-length correlation and benchmark offline feedback remain inherited limitations
Shared training effects can alter unsupported slices; no causal per-user mechanism claim from aggregate slice AUC

Round12 true within-block order beat scrambled, round13 coarse order beat duplicate in both task/shared routing. These are different mechanism contrasts, not independent replications. No failed execution appears in current trajectory index and previous_runtime_error is null.
